skeleton:
Create a production animation sprite sheet for a 2D hand-painted side-scrolling cartoon game. The first supplied reference is the game's zombie clown sprite: MATCH its drawn animation language, matte painted shading, hand-inked outlines and slightly soft storybook texture. The second reference is the current game scene with a skeleton: REPLACE its disjointed articulated-puppet anatomy with a cohesive, charming WHOLE-BODY drawn character. Do not reproduce the background or other characters.
Output exactly 24 full character animation frames arranged in 4 columns and 6 rows on a transparent background. Each cell has identical dimensions, generous empty gutters, same character scale and feet baseline. NO text, numbers, grid lines, shadows under the cells or scenery. Each frame is ONE complete painted pose, never isolated body pieces except when the character collapses in the last two rows.
Character: a cute, slightly mischievous cartoon skeleton facing LEFT in three-quarter side view; large rounded skull with two simple deep dark oval eye sockets, small triangular nose hole, short rounded teeth, compact oval rib cage, rounded pelvis, short stout limbs with simplified continuous connected bones and broad skeletal feet. Muted aged ivory with cool lavender-grey shadows, not glaring white. No clown costume, no hat, no shoes. Skull about one third of standing height; expressive body but NOT skeletal marionette sticks. Preserve the SAME skull, anatomy, scale, proportions and painted shading across all frames.
Read frames left to right, rows top to bottom:
Frames 0-7 (rows 1-2): seamless 8-frame WALK LEFT loop. Easy deliberate steps with alternating planted feet, soft knee bends, torso bob, slight skull tilt and opposite arm swing. Eight DISTINCT evenly spaced phases, no extreme high knees or crossed spaghetti legs. Same feet baseline and body center across cells.
Frames 8-15 (rows 3-4): rib-throw attack. 8 hand begins moving to ribcage; 9 hand touches chest; 10 hand pantomimes grasping a rib; 11 pulls a small curved ivory rib out in front; 12 winds up the arm behind head holding curved rib; 13 raises bent arm behind head; 14 swings arm forward toward LEFT, extended open hand releasing the rib (no detached projectile, game adds it); 15 settles back into relaxed ready stance. Rib cage stays intact, the rib is a conjured prop. Feet stay planted.
Frames 16-23 (rows 5-6): defeated skeleton crumbles to the GROUND in eight progressive full-frame stages. 16 stagger and knees buckle; 17 ribs and shoulders start separating while head drops; 18 arms, ribs and legs disconnect, falling downward, skull sinking; 19 disconnected bones falling and skull close to ground; 20 skull and ribcage hit ground and bones bounce; 21 low scattered bone pile with skull sideways; 22 pile finishes settling; 23 final motionless pile of skull, ribs, pelvis and limb bones lying on ground. NO intact standing skeleton in final frames. All fallen pieces remain within their own cell and rest on the same floor line as standing feet. Same bone sizes in every frame; do not scale the pile up. Do not hide it in smoke. Transparent alpha everywhere outside the artwork.
fog: Create a transparent raster game environment overlay: one wide continuous patch of LOW-LYING CEMETERY MIST, painted by hand in the subdued grey-lavender and blue-grey palette of the supplied cemetery environment. Wispy horizontal drifts close to the ground, layered soft flowing curls and thin irregular translucent veils, varied thickness, strongest in a low central band, completely feathered to transparent at all edges. The mist must be subtle and semi-transparent, letting the landscape show through. Quiet dusk graveyard atmosphere, matte painted anime/storybook art. Landscape format about 3:1. No sky, trees, graves, characters, ground, lighting rays, bright white puffy clouds, symbols or text. Alpha transparent background. This is just a fog overlay to scroll slowly across the existing scene; avoid hard edges or an opaque rectangle.
